newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Grupo Condumex to buy 52 pct of Latinca.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Grupo Condumex to buy 52 pct of Latinca.

text.p: Mexican electrical hardware makers Grupo Condumex SA de CV (Codumex) plan to buy a majority stake in cable manufacturer Conductores Latincasa SA de CV (Latinca), a source told Reuters on Wednesday.
"The purchase has yet to be settled, it's for 52 percent of Latinca's equity. The deal would be worth around $40 million," a source close to the company said, who requested anonymity.
The deal was subject to approval by Mexico's Monopolies Commission.
"The purchase may be (formally) announced in the coming weeks," the source added.
Condumex's holding company, Grupo Carso, had previously acquired a temporary five percent stake in Latinca.
Analysts generally welcomed the deal, saying it was in line with Grupo Carso's traditional strategy of buying small companies and improving their fortunes.
"We view the probable acquisition as positive," a report by Mexico City Valores Finamex (Vafin) brokerage said on Wednesday.
"It will solidify Condumex's dominance in Mexico and strengthen its presence abroad, expanding the company's product line and broadening its customer base," the report added.

Vafin estimated that as a result of the Latinca acquisition, Condumex's 1997 sales would increase by 14.6 percent in real terms to eight billion pesos, with the operating margin declining slightly to 19.5 percent from 19.7 percent in 1996.

"We view...(the) acquisition as a positive move for Carso Industrial, one that keeps it on track with its business strategy of making acquisitions and growing in strategic sectors," a Bear Stearns report said.
Bear Stearns meanwhile estimated the deal would "add approximately eight percent in incremental sales" to Condumex and situated the 1997 operating margin at "close to" 19.7 percent.
Vafin said it continued to rate Grupo Carso as a buy.
Grupo Carso shares were up 65 centavos to 44.90 pesos at midday trade on Wednesday.
